title: PCP discovery document
description: The JSON served at /.well-known/pcp.json (SPEC §2). A context document describes one context, carries its MCP endpoint and points at its OAuth protected resource metadata (SPEC §2.5, §3.2). A root document describes a multi-context host and carries a context URL template instead.

pcp_version.description: The PCP version the server implements. A v0.3 server emits "0.3".

multi_context.description: true in the root document of a multi-context host (SPEC §2.2). Absent or false in a context document.

context_url_template.description: Root documents only. An RFC 6570 level 1 URI Template with exactly one variable, {context}, that expands to a context's base URL. The context document is at <base>/.well-known/pcp.json.

kind.description: Context documents only. What the context is (SPEC §1.2).

controller_type.description: Context documents only. The type of the context's controller (SPEC §1.2, §9.2): human or org. REQUIRED for kind work; MUST be human for kind personal.

mcp_endpoint.description: Context documents only. The context's MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint. It is also the context's OAuth resource identifier: the resource of its protected resource metadata, character for character (SPEC §3.2).

resource_metadata.description: Context documents only. URL of the context's OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), normally the path-suffixed well-known URL of mcp_endpoint. The same URL appears in every WWW-Authenticate challenge of the endpoint (SPEC §3.2).

alternate_endpoints.description: Context documents only. Other URLs at which the same context's MCP endpoint is served, each with its own context document and protected resource metadata (SPEC §9.8).

authorization_server.description: Deprecated. A hint kept from v0.2: if present it MUST equal the first entry of authorization_servers in the context's protected resource metadata. Clients discover the authorization server from that metadata (SPEC §2.3, §3.2), never from this field.

server_card.description: URL of the MCP server card for this context's endpoint, when the server publishes one.

profile.description: Which profile document the context has (SPEC §4). Defaults: "core" for personal and work contexts, "team" for team contexts.

profile_extensions.description: Profile extension namespaces present in this context (SPEC §4.5).

connections.description: Connection ids available in this context (SPEC §6.4).

extensions.description: Tool extensions the server implements, by reverse-DNS id (SPEC §6.5).

features.description: Optional parts of the model this context uses (SPEC §1.4).

conformance.description: Conformance profiles the server claims for this context (SPEC §10). A claim is a statement the conformance suite can check, not a description.

export.description: true is a claim that the server meets SPEC §8 for this context: a full export and an import of its own format. Servers MUST NOT emit true otherwise.

encryption.description: Who holds the keys and who can read plaintext (SPEC §2.4). Indexes, embeddings, caches and other derived data count as content and are covered by the same declaration.

key_custody.description: host: the host holds keys that decrypt the context without any principal's involvement. user: keys are wrapped by secrets only principals, and clients they authorized, hold; the host decrypts only while serving a request a principal authorized, and keeps neither keys nor plaintext afterwards (SPEC §9.1.3). device: plaintext and keys exist only on principals' devices; the host stores ciphertext (SPEC §9.1.4).

readable_by.description: Every party that can obtain plaintext. principals: authorized principals through their clients (always listed). host_in_request: the host, only while serving an authorized request. host: the host, at any time. escrow: a third party holding a recovery share.

e2e.description: End-to-end encrypted. MAY be true only when key_custody is device. Defaults to false.
